correctness.rationale: A complete three-onset-stage proof holds for all real 0<x<y<=1, 0<w<1, 0<lambda<1. Strict monotonicity of the partial-runoff ratio gives at most one crossing before both zones run. An exact weighted-reciprocal identity yields a fully-wet cubic with precisely one positive root by coefficient signs and Descartes. Continuity and a negative large-rain asymptote join regimes, yielding exactly one global crossing. A directly checked second derivative gives strict convexity for rainfall up to 1/(1+lambda) and a limiting sharp infimum; a constructive parameter sequence makes the crossing unbounded. Standalone tests check exact rational example and 2400 configurations, supporting but not proving universal result.

value.rationale: Distributed area-average storm runoff versus runoff from area-average curve number is a motivated choice in catchment calculations. The finding completely classifies the sign for every two-land-cover mixture and every storm depth, resolves numerical ambiguity by one crossing, supplies an exact cubic and a sharp universal positive lower bound, and demonstrates why no universal empirical high-rainfall cap can hold. This is more than routine first-order Jensen and does not claim the known sign reversal itself as new. Its limit is an idealized two-zone mathematical model, not physical runoff calibration.
